extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of 18th-century English essays; literary scholars; writers interested in characterization and essay techniques
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and exemplars for composing short comic/period essays and character sketches in the style of The Spectator (early-18th-century English satire), including techniques of characterization, allegory, audience tailoring, and theatrical observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theatre size and acoustics
rubrics_metrics.description: The house was too large, and its architecture swallowed up the voices of the actors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and scale must suit spoken drama: overly large houses and certain architectural choices can make words inaudible. Practical fixes (historical example) included contracting the width of the theatre and lowering an enormously high ceiling to make plays audible; physical architecture should be matched to theatrical needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programming must match audience taste
rubrics_metrics.description: They opened with a translated opera set to Italian music, which ran only for three nights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select repertoire that aligns with local audience expectations. Concessions to a fashionable taste (e.g., Italian opera) may fail if the audience or the venue's social catchment doesn't support it; initial programming decisions strongly affect early reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding model: aristocratic subscription for ventures
rubrics_metrics.description: Thirty persons of quality having subscribed a hundred pounds each towards the cost of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large cultural projects can be financed by subscription from patrons of quality; the composition of funders (social class, geographic convenience) and their expectations influence the venture's programming and success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management & talent arrangements determine success
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreements to allow a manager to draw what actors he pleased from another house and divide profits; compacts between houses were made and broken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Business arrangements—who controls the license, who supplies actors, profit-sharing, and whether houses coordinate or compete—shape a company's fortunes. Stability of management compacts and clarity of arrangements matter for sustained success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorial purpose: satisfy your own mind
rubrics_metrics.description: It is endless and frivolous Pursuit to act by any other Rule than the Care of satisfying our own Minds in what we do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An author's primary rule should be to satisfy their own judgment and design rather than obsess over external reputation or transient opinion. Work produced this way is steadier than work written to chase fame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not be anxious about reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the worst Way in the World to Fame, to be too anxious about it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excessive concern for reputation distracts and diminishes work; authors are advised to be 'very negligent of the Consequences' and careful of their design instead. This is prescriptive guidance on authorial temperament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of detached observation and solitude
rubrics_metrics.description: To be exempt from the Passions with which others are tormented, is the only pleasing Solitude. 'I am never less alone than when alone.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detached, silent observation (including self-imposed reticence in public) yields sharper perception of character, manners, and the inner life of people; solitude is a resource for penetration and mirthful reflection useful to an essayist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor style and voice to specific audience segments
rubrics_metrics.description: When it is a Woman's Day, in my Works, I shall endeavour at a Stile and Air suitable to their Understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust tone, style, and subject matter to particular readerships (here, addressing women in a mode suited to them). The writer plans distinct 'days' or pieces aimed at different constituencies—an explicit audience-targeting strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use allegory and personification to explain abstract public matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Methoughts I returned to the Great Hall... a beautiful Virgin seated on a Throne of Gold. Her Name... was Publick Credit. The Walls... were hung with many Acts of Parliament written in Golden Letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To render complex civic/economic issues vivid, employ allegory (personification of abstract concepts, symbolic props like Acts of Parliament, money-bags, phantom dances). Allegory structures argument and makes abstract threats and remedies tangible to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dramatic juxtaposition of opposing forces for rhetorical effect
rubrics_metrics.description: There entered half a dozen of the most hideous Phantoms... the first Couple were Tyranny and Anarchy, the second were Bigotry and Atheism, the third the Genius of a Common-Wealth, and a young Man... with a Sword... and a Spunge in his left Hand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pair contrasting abstractions as dramatic 'couples' or dances to highlight threats and tensions; staging opposing figures together emphasizes their conflict and impact on the central allegorical figure (e.g., Publick Credit). Use visual/motion imagery (dance, entrance, fainting) for persuasive rhetoric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization: likable eccentricities grounded in sense
rubrics_metrics.description: He is a Gentleman that is very singular in his Behaviour, but his Singularities proceed from his good Sense... this Humour creates him no Enemies, for he does nothing with Sourness or Obstinacy; and his being unconfined to Modes and Forms, makes him but the readier and more capable to please and oblige all who know him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create eccentric characters whose oddities arise from good sense and benevolence rather than petulance; such singularities make them charming rather than offensive. Eccentricity plus good nature produces comic affection rather than hostility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use concrete, recurrent details to define comic persona
rubrics_metrics.description: He continues to wear a Coat and Doublet of the same Cut that were in Fashion at the Time of his Repulse... has been in and out twelve Times since he first wore it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define characters with specific, repeated visual or behavioral quirks (anachronistic costume, persistent habits) to create memorable, gently comic sketches; recurring details signal personality and history without long exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrast learned taste with practical ignorance as a comic device
rubrics_metrics.description: He knows Aristotle and Longinus better than Littleton or Cooke... The Father sends up every Post Questions relating to Marriage-Articles, Leases, and Tenures... No one ever took him for a Fool, but none... know he has a great deal of Wit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make characters pleasantly paradoxical by giving them high literary or critical taste but limited practical knowledge; this produces conversational wit and ironic comic effect (a critic who is not a practitioner).

rubrics_metrics.name: Portray modesty as an internal obstacle with sympathetic tone
rubrics_metrics.description: A Person of great Courage, good Understanding, but Invincible Modesty... he has quitted a Way of Life in which no Man can rise suitably to his Merit... A strict Honesty and an even regular Behaviour, are in themselves Obstacles to him...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use modesty and integrity as traits that impede worldly advancement; present such characters sympathetically, showing their frank reflections and military/adventurous anecdotes to make them engaging rather than merely ineffectual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use proverbs and pithy maxims to characterize social types
rubrics_metrics.description: He abounds in several frugal Maxims, amongst which the greatest Favourite is, 'A Penny saved is a Penny got.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign stock sayings, commercial maxims, or catchphrases to figures (merchants, gallants) to quickly convey outlook and values; laconic maxims function as shorthand character markers and can be mildly comic in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: A critic character can function to elevate dramatic performance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Time of the Play is his Hour of Business; exactly at five he passes... It is for the Good of the Audience when he is at a Play, for the Actors have an Ambition to please him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a knowledgeable critic figure whose presence pressures performers to improve; such a character both flatters and regulates the cultural scene, and provides a narrative device to show actors' ambition and the value of good taste.
